message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering public vulnerability information reported or materially updated in the last 24 hours before the scheduled run on 2026-07-21 at 05:10 IST. Credible, source-dated findings were found for Ubuntu, nginx, Apache HTTP Server, and Wget. A few recently crawled Fortinet/FortiOS pages were excluded because Fortinet's own timelines showed older publication or update dates.

**Finding 1: nginx vulnerabilities fixed in Ubuntu packages**

- Product: Nginx / Ubuntu nginx package
- Issue: CVE-2026-42533, CVE-2026-56434, and CVE-2026-60005
- Severity: Major for CVE-2026-42533; Medium for CVE-2026-56434 and CVE-2026-60005 according to the nginx security advisory page.
- Description: Canonical published an nginx update on 2026-07-20 for issues that could cause denial of service, possible arbitrary code execution, or sensitive information exposure depending on module and configuration.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes both Nginx and Ubuntu, and the Ubuntu notice explicitly names the nginx package for supported Ubuntu releases.
- Source: Ubuntu USN-8563-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8563-1 ; nginx security advisories: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html

**Finding 2: Apache HTTP Server vulnerabilities fixed in Ubuntu packages**

- Product: Apache HTTP Server / Ubuntu apache2 package
- Issue: Multiple CVEs, including CVE-2026-33007, CVE-2026-33523, CVE-2026-33857, CVE-2026-34032, CVE-2026-34355, CVE-2026-34356, CVE-2026-42535, CVE-2026-42536, CVE-2026-43951, CVE-2026-44119, CVE-2026-44185, CVE-2026-44186, CVE-2026-44631, CVE-2026-48913, and CVE-2026-49975.
- Severity: Apache rates the related upstream issues mostly Low or Moderate; Canonical did not state a single overall severity in the USN.
- Description: Canonical published Apache HTTP Server package fixes on 2026-07-20 for issues involving denial of service, information disclosure, HTTP response splitting, privilege-related .htaccess behavior, and possible arbitrary code execution in crafted configuration scenarios.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Apache HTTP Server and Ubuntu, and the Ubuntu notice explicitly names the apache2 package.
- Source: Ubuntu USN-8571-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8571-1 ; Apache HTTP Server 2.4 vulnerability list: https://httpd.apache.org/security/vulnerabilities_24.html

**Finding 3: Ubuntu Linux kernel vulnerabilities**

- Product: Ubuntu Linux kernel packages
- Issue: Multiple kernel CVEs across USN-8567-1, USN-8569-1, and USN-8570-1, including Dirty Frag-related CVEs and Fragnesia-related CVEs cited in Canonical's notices.
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Canonical in the reviewed notices.
- Description: Canonical published several Linux kernel updates on 2026-07-20 for Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and 22.04 LTS variants, covering local information disclosure, privilege escalation, possible container escape, denial of service, and broad kernel subsystem fixes.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Ubuntu, and the notices apply to Ubuntu kernel packages.
- Source: Ubuntu USN-8567-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8567-1 ; USN-8569-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8569-1 ; USN-8570-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8570-1

**Finding 4: Wget SSRF issue fixed in Ubuntu packages**

- Product: Ubuntu wget package
- Issue: CVE-2026-15146
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Canonical in the reviewed notice.
- Description: Canonical published a Wget update on 2026-07-20 for improper validation of FTP passive-mode PASV response IP addresses, which could let a malicious server redirect Wget data connections to unintended internal or local network resources.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Ubuntu; Wget is an Ubuntu package covered by Canonical's security notice across supported and ESM releases.
- Source: Ubuntu USN-8572-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8572-1

**Additional Ubuntu package notices from the same window**

Canonical also published 2026-07-20 Ubuntu notices for libde265 (multiple media parsing CVEs), SQLite (CVE-2026-50812 and CVE-2026-50813), PHP (CVE-2026-12184 and CVE-2026-14355), libXfont, and rlottie. These are relevant to Ubuntu estates where those packages are installed, but they are less directly mapped to the named product list than nginx and Apache HTTP Server. Sources: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8573-1 , https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8565-1 , https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8564-1 , https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8560-1 , https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8559-1

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for systems running exposed nginx or Apache HTTP Server packages, and for Ubuntu kernel update/reboot planning. No fresh, clearly product-matched advisories were verified in this run for the other monitored products.
